issue.title: [codex] Enforce deletion author checks
issue.body: ## Summary Fixes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#94. This enforces the NIP-09 deletion authorization rule inside MLS group message handling: - Require the kind-5 deletion author to match the cached target message/reaction author before mutating local cache state. - Preserve kind-5 deletion rows as audit/orphan records, but reject unauthorized orphan replay when the target message later arrives. - Add an author predicate to `AggregatedMessage::mark_deleted` so the DB update is guarded too. - Apply the same author check to outgoing optimistic deletion handling so local UI state cannot be rewritten for another author's target. ## Verification - Confirmed the issue was real with a red regression test: `test_handle_mls_message_rejects_cross_author_deletion` failed before the fix because the target was marked deleted. - `just test-unit` passed: 1737 unit tests + doctests. - `just precommit-quick` passed. - `just docker-up` passed. - `just precommit` passed, including integration tests. - `just docker-down` completed after validation. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Deletions are now author-scoped—only the original message/reaction author can delete their content * Orphaned deletion tracking/cleanup now respects author scoping for accuracy * Prevented unauthorized reaction deletions and tightened outgoing deletion checks * Cascade rollback restores targets using stored deletion-event mappings * Chat list updates emit “last message deleted” only when truly removed * **Tests** * Expanded coverage for cross-author deletion, orphaned-deletion application, and reaction scenarios [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/803)

issue.title: Harden retry backoff in event processor: cap delay, add jitter, and use overflow-safe math
issue.body:
Summary
The current retry backoff is purely exponential, which risks overflow and synchronized retries ("stampedes"). We should harden the strategy by capping the delay, adding light jitter, and ensuring overflow-safe arithmetic. Include the event ID in retry logs for traceability.

Context
- Requested during review of PR #340 (Feat/global user subs).
- Requester: @jgmontoya
- PR: https://github.com/parres-hq/whitenoise/pull/340
- Discussion: https://github.com/parres-hq/whitenoise/pull/340#discussion_r2317334772

Scope
- Retry scheduling for event processing (keep changes out of PR #340; track and deliver in a separate PR).

Acceptance criteria
- Exponential backoff uses overflow-safe arithmetic and clamps to a sensible maximum delay.
- Add small jitter per event to avoid thundering herd effects.
- Retry warnings/logs include the event ID for traceability.
- Unit tests cover delay capping, jitter bounds, and absence of overflow at high attempts.
- Consider simple configurability for max delay and jitter percentage (constants or config).

Notes
Please link the implementing PR back to this issue upon submission

type.name: Feature

issue.body:
# Context

Similar problem as the one described in #788 but for the case in which I'm removed and already in the chat, The hack used was listening to the chat list stream cause that one had an event for RemovedFromGroup and   LeftGroup, but chat stream didn't


# Solution
At first with @jgmontoya we thought about adding a new event to the chat stream, but then we realized that this kind of event is not really related to a message, and chat stream updates until now are event related to a message. This update is more generic, related to the group, So we are more inclined to have a new group stream for this general info.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Track skipped reaction targets through the rollback path.**

This `continue` fixes the optimistic delete, but the publish-failure path still restores **every** tagged reaction in `cascade_deletion_failure()`. If an unauthorized deletion of another user’s reaction fails to publish, the parent summary gets that reaction added again even though it was never removed, which can double-count the reaction in the UI. Please make rollback conditional on targets that were actually mutated (for example by recording applied target IDs or restoring only rows marked deleted by this deletion).

in the deletion path (around AggregatedMessage::find_reaction_by_id and the
continue when reaction.author != mdk_message.pubkey) skips unauthorized targets
but later cascade_deletion_failure() restores all tagged reactions; change the
delete flow to record which target_ids were actually mutated (e.g. collect
applied_target_ids in the code that marks rows deleted inside the loop) and make
cascade_deletion_failure() (or the rollback caller) only restore those recorded

issue.title: Fix message_delivery_status scope: add account_pubkey to primary key
issue.body:
## Bug

`message_delivery_status` is keyed by `(message_id, mls_group_id)` and tracks sender-local state (send attempts, retry count, failure reason). It has no `account_pubkey` column.

If two local accounts are members of the same group, their delivery state collides — one account's retry/failure state can bleed into the other account's UI.

## Fix

Add `account_pubkey` to the primary key. Migration should:

1. Create `message_delivery_status_v2` with `(account_pubkey, message_id, mls_group_id)` as the key and the same other columns
2. Copy rows from the old table, filling `account_pubkey` by joining against `accounts_groups` on `mls_group_id` (if multiple local accounts are in the same group, copy the row once per account)
3. Drop the old table and rename v2
4. Update all read/write call sites to include `account_pubkey`

## Scope

- Schema migration
- Update model types and DB access code
- Test: create two local accounts in the same group, verify their delivery state is independent

## What this PR does

Lands the **session and projection rearchitecture** — a refactor that
restructures White Noise around explicit account-scoped sessions, projection-owning
services, and per-account SQLite databases. The work was executed across 19 numbered
phases, each landed as its own reviewed PR; this PR merges the full series from
`arch-refactor` into `master`.

**Scope:** 44 commits · 337 files · +42,350 / −17,302 

The design is fully documented in-repo:

- [`docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md`](docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md) — target architecture
- [`docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md`](docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md) — phase-by-phase plan
- [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md) — three-tier test model


Closes #739.

---

## Why

The pre-refactor codebase had a single `Whitenoise` global singleton with ~25 fields
and `impl` blocks spread across 37+ files. That shape produced three structural
problems:

1. **"Where does this go?"** Core files had grown past 2,000 lines; contributors
   couldn't tell where new code belonged or whether something similar already existed.
2. **Account scope was a convention, not a guarantee.** Every account-mutating
   method accepted `pubkey: PublicKey` as an argument; the compiler couldn't catch a
   wrong-pubkey bug. `message_delivery_status` already had a real scope bug where
   sender-local state bled across accounts in the same group.
3. **The singleton blocked testing.** `Whitenoise::get_instance()` returned a
   process-wide static. Parallel tests with isolated state were impossible. Swapping
   a service for a test double was impossible. Integration tests required
   logout → sleep → reset-client → wipe-database → sleep between scenarios.

The relay-control-plane rearchitecture had already solved the same problem at the
transport layer (one shared `nostr-sdk::Client` split into four dedicated planes).
This PR applies the same treatment to the domain layer.

---

## What changes

### 1. `AccountSession` is the new account-scoped handle

Account-scoped state has a typed owner. Login creates a session; logout drops it.
Account identity is baked into the handle, not passed as an argument.

```rust
// before
whitenoise.send_message_to_group(&account, &group_id, content).await?;
whitenoise.leave_group(&account, &group_id).await?;
whitenoise.follow_user(&account, &target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.resolve_user(&pubkey).await?;

// after
let session = whitenoise.session(account_pubkey)?;
session.messages().send_to_group(&group_id, content).await?;
session.groups().leave(&group_id).await?;
session.social().follow_user(&target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.shared().user_directory().resolve(&pubkey).await?;
```

`session.messages()`, `session.groups()`, etc. return lightweight `View<'_>` types
that borrow the session — no Arc cycles, no separate service construction. Views
live in `src/whitenoise/session/`, one file per concern.

### 2. Four explicit state categories

Every piece of state now belongs to exactly one of:

| Category | Owner | Mutation rule |
|---|---|---|
| MDK authority | `AccountSession.mdk` (cached `Arc<MDK<_>>`) | MDK only |
| Shared app state | `SharedServices` (user directory, relays, app settings, media blob cache, …) | Shared services own writes; sessions read |
| Account-scoped app state | `AccountSession.repos` over `AccountDatabase` | Session services only |
| Projections | Declared builder + reader pair | Builders write directly to projection tables, readers query |

### 3. The singleton is gone

`Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. `Whitenoise` is constructed at startup
(FRB init, CLI daemon, tests) and passed by reference. `OnceCell`/`OnceLock` are
now reserved for process-level concerns only (tracing init, keyring store).

### 4. Per-account SQLite databases

Storage moved from one shared DB to a shared DB + one DB per account:

```
data/
├── shared.sqlite                    (registry + shared caches + operational state)
├── account_<hex_pubkey>.sqlite      (one per local account)
└── mdk_<hex_pubkey>/                (MDK's own per-account DB, unchanged)
```

Tables now in the per-account DB: `account_settings`, `account_follows`,
`accounts_groups`, `drafts`, `push_registrations`, `group_push_tokens`,
`published_key_packages`, `published_events`, `aggregated_messages`,
`message_delivery_status`, `media_references`, `mute_list`, account-scoped
`processed_events`.

Tables remaining in `shared.sqlite`: `accounts` (registry), `users`,
`relays`, `user_relays`, `cached_graph_users`, `group_information`,
`media_blobs` (shared blob cache), `relay_status`, `relay_events`, global
`processed_events`, `app_settings`.

Consequence: account deletion is `fs::remove_file` on the account DB plus
removing the MDK directory. No multi-table row cleanup. No chance of leftover
state.

### 5. SQLx migrations replaced with an in-tree Rust framework

`sqlx::migrate!` no longer drives schema. The Rust framework lets us:
- Apply migrations against either the shared DB or each per-account DB,
- Rebaseline the bootstrap (v17–v22 + v29 are now baked into
  `fresh_account_schema` per PR #790) so new accounts open a single `CREATE`
  rather than replay every historical migration,
- Run cross-DB ordering with explicit dependencies (see PR #785).

### 6. CLI extracted to a workspace crate

`crates/whitenoise-cli/` is now its own workspace member with its own
`Cargo.toml`. The core library no longer pulls in `clap`, `dirs`, or
`rpassword`. `wn` / `wnd` binaries live in the CLI crate. Shared deps
(`mdk-core`, `nostr-sdk`, `tokio`, …) are declared once in
`[workspace.dependencies]` so the core crate and CLI can't silently diverge
on git-pinned revisions.

### 7. BroadcastHub consolidation

The four structurally identical streaming managers (chat list, messages,
notifications, group state, user) are unified behind a generic
`BroadcastHub<K, V>` (Phase 17, PR #765). Streaming entry points haven't
changed for consumers.

---

## Phase log

| Phase | PR | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #743 | `AccountSession` + `AccountManager` scaffolding, startup restore, MDK caching |
| 2 | (PR included) | Per-account guards and cancellation moved to session |
| 3 / 3b | #753, #755, #756 | Scoped relay handles; `AccountInboxPlane` ownership on session |
| 4 | #754 | `AccountRepositories` scaffold |
| 5 | #761 | View pattern: drafts, follows, settings migrated |
| 6 + 7 | #760 | Message read/search + send/retry/projection write path; `message_delivery_status` scope bug fix |
| 8 | #763 | Group read operations |
| 9 | #766 | Group member/data mutation operations |
| 10 | #769 | `create_group` and welcome delivery on session |
| 11 | #772 | Group media operations on `MediaOps` |
| 12 | #764 | Memberships (`accounts_groups`) → `MembershipOps` |
| 13 | #767 | Push notification ops → `PushOps` |
| 14 | #768 | Key packages + chat list reads on session |
| 15 | #770 | Session-scoped event dispatch |
| 16a | #773 | `Arc<SharedServices>` holder (singleton still present) |
| 16b | #779 | Singleton killed; `Whitenoise` is constructed and passed in |
| 16c | #780 | Post-singleton cleanup |
| 17 | #765 | `BroadcastHub` generic for streaming managers |
| 18a | #776 | `SharedDatabase` + `AccountDatabase` newtypes; cross-scope FK audit |
| 18b | #787 | `media_files` → `media_blobs` (shared) + `media_references` (per-account) |
| 18c | #786 | Simple per-account tables moved to per-account DB |
| 18d | #792 | Membership + push tables → per-account DB |
| 18e | #796 | Message projection tables + chat-list join logic → per-account DB |
| — | #783, #785, #790 | SQLx → Rust migration framework; ordering; v31 rebaseline |
| — | #789 | `media_references` to per-account DB |
| — | #810 | `mute_list` per-account (m0042 + m0043) |
| 19 | #774 | CLI extracted to `crates/whitenoise-cli` |
| Cleanup | #818 | Remove deprecated `Whitenoise` facades; migrate remaining callers to `AccountSession` |
| Master sync / fixes | #782, #801, #812, #816, #817, #820, #795 | Master integrations + fixes for push tokens, session-restore ordering, `file_metadata` BLOB decode, MIP-04 v2 integration tests |

---

## Breaking changes for downstream consumers

Consumers of the public Rust API (notably the Flutter app via FRB):

- `Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. Construct a `Whitenoise` at app
  init and hold a reference.
- Account-scoped methods are removed from `Whitenoise` and moved onto
  `AccountSession`. Call sites change from
  `wn.method(&account, …)` to `wn.session(account.pubkey)?.area().method(…)`.
- Account deletion now removes a single SQLite file rather than running
  multi-table cleanup.
- Storage layout on disk changes — see migration notes below.

## Migration / on-disk compatibility

- Existing single-DB installations are migrated forward by the Rust migration
  framework. Per-account tables are physically moved into per-account DBs as
  part of the 18-series migrations.
- The fresh-install schema is rebaselined to v31 (PR #790); fresh accounts no
  longer replay v17–v22 / v29 historical migrations.
- Cross-scope foreign keys (e.g. `accounts_groups → accounts`,
  `drafts → group_information`) are enforced at the application layer post-split.
  See the cross-scope FK audit in the module-level doc comments of
  `database/shared_db.rs` and `database/account_db.rs`.

---

## Testing

Testing transitions to a three-tier model (see
[`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md)):

- **Tier 1 — Unit tests:** in-memory `AccountDatabase` + individually
  constructed services. Cover services, repos, views, projection logic, chat
  list ordering, message aggregation, group membership CRUD, drafts, settings,
  follows, key-package lifecycle. Run with `just test`. Parallel, fast, no
  infrastructure.
- **Tier 2 — In-process integration (MockRelay):** full in-process Nostr
  relay (WebSocket + in-memory store + NIP-01/42). Multi-instance tests like
  "Alice sends, Bob receives" are now possible. Each test owns its own
  `Whitenoise` instances; no shared state.
- **Tier 3 — Docker integration tests:** retained only for scenarios that need
  a real Blossom media server (`chat_media_upload`). Run with `just int-test`.

The scenario-by-scenario migration map is in [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md).

## Test plan (for this PR)

- [ ] CI: fmt + clippy (`-D warnings`) + docs build clean
- [ ] CI: unit tests pass on Linux + macOS-latest + macOS-14
- [ ] CI: coverage non-regression check
- [ ] CI: integration tests (Docker) green
- [ ] Manual: fresh install on a clean data dir — identity create, join group,
      send/receive, restart, verify persistence
- [ ] Manual: upgrade from a master-shaped data dir — verify per-account DB
      split applies cleanly and no rows are lost (accounts, groups, drafts,
      follows, mute list, push registrations, message projections)
- [ ] Manual: account deletion removes only that account's DB + MDK directory
- [ ] Manual: parallel `just test` runs are stable (no singleton contention)
- [ ] Spot-check: no `Whitenoise::get_instance()` callers anywhere in `src/`
      or `crates/`

issue.title: Merge master into arch-refactor (real two-parent merge — don't squash)
issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/7bcd227211a0a07194683a700602d5e214acb8cee7390029e820220cb350861d.png)

**MERGE THIS PR VIA "Create a merge commit". DO NOT SQUASH. DO NOT REBASE.**

The whole point of this PR is preserving the two-parent property of commit `d914166b`. Squash-merging throws away the ancestry link, and the next "merge master into arch-refactor" PR faces the same 48k-line conflict storm we just cleared. Future master→arch-refactor catch-ups should also use "Create a merge commit".

## What this does

Brings `origin/master` into `arch-refactor` as a real two-parent merge commit. Every prior catch-up PR was squash-merged, which is why this one was huge: git had no record that any previous merge had happened, so an entire month of master divergence (24 commits, 312 files, ~48k churn lines) replayed as conflicts.

After this lands correctly, the merge base jumps forward to today's master tip. The next catch-up only sees commits master makes from here on.

## Resolution policy

Three rules drove every conflict:

1. Keep arch's architecture: session API, per-account databases, `Arc<SharedServices>`, Rust migration framework.
2. Absorb every feature master shipped over the last month.
3. Avoid the singleton unless strictly necessary.

47 conflicted files. The mute_list trio absorbed cleanly into arch's existing `session.mute_list()` API — block/unblock had byte-equivalent NIP-51 logic on both sides. The database files were take-HEAD because arch already lives in the per-account-DB and Rust-migration world. The big files (`mod.rs`, `push_notifications.rs`, `key_packages.rs`) resolved by verifying each master feature has a session equivalent before take-HEAD.

## Master features ported onto session shape

- `session.membership().for_group(g).accept()` and `.decline()` now share/remove the local push token. This bridges master's `accept_account_group` / `decline_account_group` flow into the session API.

## Carried forward intentionally

- `KeyPackageLookup::Incompatible` stays as a unit variant (arch shape). Master's `Incompatible { error: WhitenoiseError }` diagnostic-info propagation is dropped. Can be re-added later by widening the variant and updating six match arms.
- `session.pending_push_token_responses` is now dead code — only the shared map is read in production. Worth a follow-up cleanup PR.

## Checks

- `just precommit-quick` clean
- `just test` clean: 1751 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped

## Marmots

This marmot patiently untangled a month of crossed ropes so the next marmot walks through cleanly. Future marmots reviewing this colony's merge button: **Create a merge commit**.

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

issue.title: Merge master into arch-refactor (post-#822)
issue.body:
## What this PR does

Brings master's content into `arch-refactor` so PR #821 (arch-refactor → master) can land cleanly.

PR #822 ("Merge master into arch-refactor (post-#818)") landed yesterday as a squash merge — required by this repo's `allow_merge_commit: false` policy. The squash collapsed the merge ancestry, leaving master NOT an ancestor of arch-refactor and PR #821 still showing 24 commits of conflicts.

issue.title: Merge master into arch-refactor (post-#818)
issue.body:
## What this PR does

Brings `arch-refactor` (currently at `ee30f7a` — Danny's #818 deprecated-facade removal) onto a branch that has the full master tip integrated, and fixes the CLI dispatch layer that #818 left broken.

## Commits

1. **`d8a59fe` — Merge `arch-refactor` into the post-mute-list integration branch**

   Resolves 4 small conflicts, all caused by #818's facade removal colliding with HEAD's older call sites:

   - `src/integration_tests/test_cases/group_membership/leave_group.rs` — doc comment refreshed to `AccountSession::groups().leave()`
   - `src/integration_tests/test_cases/scheduler/key_package_maintenance.rs` — three facade calls migrated to `session.key_packages().fetch_all()` / `delete_batch(...)`
   - `src/whitenoise/accounts_groups.rs` — eight test-side facade calls migrated to `session.membership().for_group(...).{get_or_create, mark_as_left, mark_as_removed}()`
   - `src/whitenoise/chat_list.rs` — drops the four deprecated facades (`get_chat_list`, `get_archived_chat_list`, `get_chat_list_item`, `build_chat_list_item`); emit path already uses `session.chat_list().build_item()`

   Master tip `59aa42c` (group state streaming + signer recovery + 22 others) was already integrated on this branch — nothing new from master is being pulled in here, just arch-refactor's post-#812 commits (`#816`, `#817`, BLOB fix, `#818`).

2. **`4dbeab1` — `fix: migrate CLI dispatch from deprecated facades to session API`**

   PR #818 removed the deprecated `Whitenoise::*` facades from the library, but missed `crates/whitenoise-cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs`, which still called 34 of them. Each call has been translated to `wn.require_session(&account.pubkey)?.area().method(...)` form. All 22 stale `#[allow(deprecated)]` attributes also removed.

   Two visibility workarounds (worth flagging for follow-up):
   - `Whitenoise::require_session` is `pub(crate)` — added a small `require_session(wn, pubkey)` helper at the top of `dispatch.rs` that wraps the public `Whitenoise::session(...)` accessor.
   - `ChatList::build_item` is `pub(crate)` — `get_chat_list_item` now scans `active()` + `archived()` for the matching `mls_group_id` instead. Less efficient but stays within the public API.

3. **`a1a903d` — `fix: restore add_members SelfRemove pre-check + hash_ref-scoped backdate`**

   Surfaced by running `just int-test` against the merged tree — two pre-existing regressions on `arch-refactor` blocked the suite:

   - **Lost pre-check (regression from #818 vs #781).** PR #781 added a per-invitee `KeyPackageCapabilities` pre-check inside `Whitenoise::add_members_to_group`: legacy peers lacking `SelfRemove` were rejected with `WhitenoiseError::KeyPackageMissingSelfRemove` before MDK saw the LeafNode. PR #818 deleted that facade and didn't port the check onto `session.groups().add_members()`, so `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario` started passing `Ok(())` for a peer it should have rejected. Restored: the pre-check now runs inside the session view (capability projection via `marmot_key_package_capabilities`, set-difference via `find_member_missing_required_proposal`, plus `map_mdk_add_members_error` defense-in-depth). Helpers were `#[cfg(test)]`-gated post-#818 since they had no callers; un-gated to `pub(crate)` so the production path can use them again. No `#[allow(dead_code)]` added.
   - **Twin-row desync in test backdate.** `AccountPublishedKeyPackagesRepo::backdate_consumed_at` scoped `UPDATE … WHERE event_id = ?`, but `mark_consumed` (production path) scopes by `key_package_hash_ref` so kind:30443 + kind:443 twins stay in sync. Result: `backdate_consumed_at_for_testing` only backdated one twin, the other kept a `consumed_at = now`, and the uncorrelated `NOT EXISTS` clause in `find_eligible_for_cleanup` saw the un-backdated twin and returned empty — `KeyPackageLifecycleTestCase` then panicked at `Key material should be marked as deleted after maintenance cleanup`. Backdate now scopes by `hash_ref` via a subquery lookup, mirroring `mark_consumed`'s shape.

   Behavior impact for reviewers: `session.groups().add_members(...)` now returns `WhitenoiseError::KeyPackageMissingSelfRemove { member_pubkey }` (or `GroupRejectedMember` for other modeled proposals) when an invitee's published KeyPackage doesn't advertise the group's required proposals. Matches the original #781 semantics; covered by `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario`.

## Why bundle them

Without the dispatch.rs migration, `cargo check -p whitenoise-cli` fails with 40 errors and the branch doesn't build; #818 should have included that cleanup. Without the third commit, `just int-test` fails on `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario` then `KeyPackageLifecycleTestCase` — both pre-existing regressions on `arch-refactor`. Bundling keeps `arch-refactor` green and unblocks PR #821.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean (0 errors)
- [x] `just precommit-quick` — fmt ✓ docs ✓ clippy ✓ dead_code ✓
- [x] `just int-test` — full integration suite (CI)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved account session handling for group management, messaging, chat operations, and media features to ensure proper authentication requirements.

* **Refactor**
  * Updated internal operation dispatching to use consistent session-based authentication across all CLI commands.

[![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/822)

issue.title: Merge master into arch-refactor (post-#818)
issue.body:
## What this PR does

Brings `arch-refactor` (currently at `ee30f7a` — Danny's #818 deprecated-facade removal) onto a branch that has the full master tip integrated, and fixes the CLI dispatch layer that #818 left broken.

## Commits

1. **`d8a59fe` — Merge `arch-refactor` into the post-mute-list integration branch**

   Resolves 4 small conflicts, all caused by #818's facade removal colliding with HEAD's older call sites:

   - `src/integration_tests/test_cases/group_membership/leave_group.rs` — doc comment refreshed to `AccountSession::groups().leave()`
   - `src/integration_tests/test_cases/scheduler/key_package_maintenance.rs` — three facade calls migrated to `session.key_packages().fetch_all()` / `delete_batch(...)`
   - `src/whitenoise/accounts_groups.rs` — eight test-side facade calls migrated to `session.membership().for_group(...).{get_or_create, mark_as_left, mark_as_removed}()`
   - `src/whitenoise/chat_list.rs` — drops the four deprecated facades (`get_chat_list`, `get_archived_chat_list`, `get_chat_list_item`, `build_chat_list_item`); emit path already uses `session.chat_list().build_item()`

   Master tip `59aa42c` (group state streaming + signer recovery + 22 others) was already integrated on this branch — nothing new from master is being pulled in here, just arch-refactor's post-#812 commits (`#816`, `#817`, BLOB fix, `#818`).

2. **`4dbeab1` — `fix: migrate CLI dispatch from deprecated facades to session API`**

   PR #818 removed the deprecated `Whitenoise::*` facades from the library, but missed `crates/whitenoise-cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs`, which still called 34 of them. Each call has been translated to `wn.require_session(&account.pubkey)?.area().method(...)` form. All 22 stale `#[allow(deprecated)]` attributes also removed.

   Two visibility workarounds (worth flagging for follow-up):
   - `Whitenoise::require_session` is `pub(crate)` — added a small `require_session(wn, pubkey)` helper at the top of `dispatch.rs` that wraps the public `Whitenoise::session(...)` accessor.
   - `ChatList::build_item` is `pub(crate)` — `get_chat_list_item` now scans `active()` + `archived()` for the matching `mls_group_id` instead. Less efficient but stays within the public API.

3. **`a1a903d` — `fix: restore add_members SelfRemove pre-check + hash_ref-scoped backdate`**

   Surfaced by running `just int-test` against the merged tree — two pre-existing regressions on `arch-refactor` blocked the suite:

   - **Lost pre-check (regression from #818 vs #781).** PR #781 added a per-invitee `KeyPackageCapabilities` pre-check inside `Whitenoise::add_members_to_group`: legacy peers lacking `SelfRemove` were rejected with `WhitenoiseError::KeyPackageMissingSelfRemove` before MDK saw the LeafNode. PR #818 deleted that facade and didn't port the check onto `session.groups().add_members()`, so `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario` started passing `Ok(())` for a peer it should have rejected. Restored: the pre-check now runs inside the session view (capability projection via `marmot_key_package_capabilities`, set-difference via `find_member_missing_required_proposal`, plus `map_mdk_add_members_error` defense-in-depth). Helpers were `#[cfg(test)]`-gated post-#818 since they had no callers; un-gated to `pub(crate)` so the production path can use them again. No `#[allow(dead_code)]` added.
   - **Twin-row desync in test backdate.** `AccountPublishedKeyPackagesRepo::backdate_consumed_at` scoped `UPDATE … WHERE event_id = ?`, but `mark_consumed` (production path) scopes by `key_package_hash_ref` so kind:30443 + kind:443 twins stay in sync. Result: `backdate_consumed_at_for_testing` only backdated one twin, the other kept a `consumed_at = now`, and the uncorrelated `NOT EXISTS` clause in `find_eligible_for_cleanup` saw the un-backdated twin and returned empty — `KeyPackageLifecycleTestCase` then panicked at `Key material should be marked as deleted after maintenance cleanup`. Backdate now scopes by `hash_ref` via a subquery lookup, mirroring `mark_consumed`'s shape.

   Behavior impact for reviewers: `session.groups().add_members(...)` now returns `WhitenoiseError::KeyPackageMissingSelfRemove { member_pubkey }` (or `GroupRejectedMember` for other modeled proposals) when an invitee's published KeyPackage doesn't advertise the group's required proposals. Matches the original #781 semantics; covered by `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario`.

## Why bundle them

Without the dispatch.rs migration, `cargo check -p whitenoise-cli` fails with 40 errors and the branch doesn't build; #818 should have included that cleanup. Without the third commit, `just int-test` fails on `AddMemberToStrictGroupRejectedScenario` then `KeyPackageLifecycleTestCase` — both pre-existing regressions on `arch-refactor`. Bundling keeps `arch-refactor` green and unblocks PR #821.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean (0 errors)
- [x] `just precommit-quick` — fmt ✓ docs ✓ clippy ✓ dead_code ✓
- [x] `just int-test` — full integration suite (CI)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved account session handling for group management, messaging, chat operations, and media features to ensure proper authentication requirements.

* **Refactor**
  * Updated internal operation dispatching to use consistent session-based authentication across all CLI commands.

[![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/822)

issue.title: refactor: session + projection rearchitecture (arch-refactor → master)
issue.body:
## What this PR does

Lands the **session and projection rearchitecture** — a refactor that
restructures White Noise around explicit account-scoped sessions, projection-owning
services, and per-account SQLite databases. The work was executed across 19 numbered
phases, each landed as its own reviewed PR; this PR merges the full series from
`arch-refactor` into `master`.

**Scope:** 44 commits · 337 files · +42,350 / −17,302 

The design is fully documented in-repo:

- [`docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md`](docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md) — target architecture
- [`docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md`](docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md) — phase-by-phase plan
- [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md) — three-tier test model


Closes #739.

---

## Why

The pre-refactor codebase had a single `Whitenoise` global singleton with ~25 fields
and `impl` blocks spread across 37+ files. That shape produced three structural
problems:

1. **"Where does this go?"** Core files had grown past 2,000 lines; contributors
   couldn't tell where new code belonged or whether something similar already existed.
2. **Account scope was a convention, not a guarantee.** Every account-mutating
   method accepted `pubkey: PublicKey` as an argument; the compiler couldn't catch a
   wrong-pubkey bug. `message_delivery_status` already had a real scope bug where
   sender-local state bled across accounts in the same group.
3. **The singleton blocked testing.** `Whitenoise::get_instance()` returned a
   process-wide static. Parallel tests with isolated state were impossible. Swapping
   a service for a test double was impossible. Integration tests required
   logout → sleep → reset-client → wipe-database → sleep between scenarios.

The relay-control-plane rearchitecture had already solved the same problem at the
transport layer (one shared `nostr-sdk::Client` split into four dedicated planes).
This PR applies the same treatment to the domain layer.

---

## What changes

### 1. `AccountSession` is the new account-scoped handle

Account-scoped state has a typed owner. Login creates a session; logout drops it.
Account identity is baked into the handle, not passed as an argument.

```rust
// before
whitenoise.send_message_to_group(&account, &group_id, content).await?;
whitenoise.leave_group(&account, &group_id).await?;
whitenoise.follow_user(&account, &target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.resolve_user(&pubkey).await?;

// after
let session = whitenoise.session(account_pubkey)?;
session.messages().send_to_group(&group_id, content).await?;
session.groups().leave(&group_id).await?;
session.social().follow_user(&target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.shared().user_directory().resolve(&pubkey).await?;
```

`session.messages()`, `session.groups()`, etc. return lightweight `View<'_>` types
that borrow the session — no Arc cycles, no separate service construction. Views
live in `src/whitenoise/session/`, one file per concern.

### 2. Four explicit state categories

Every piece of state now belongs to exactly one of:

| Category | Owner | Mutation rule |
|---|---|---|
| MDK authority | `AccountSession.mdk` (cached `Arc<MDK<_>>`) | MDK only |
| Shared app state | `SharedServices` (user directory, relays, app settings, media blob cache, …) | Shared services own writes; sessions read |
| Account-scoped app state | `AccountSession.repos` over `AccountDatabase` | Session services only |
| Projections | Declared builder + reader pair | Builders write directly to projection tables, readers query |

### 3. The singleton is gone

`Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. `Whitenoise` is constructed at startup
(FRB init, CLI daemon, tests) and passed by reference. `OnceCell`/`OnceLock` are
now reserved for process-level concerns only (tracing init, keyring store).

### 4. Per-account SQLite databases

Storage moved from one shared DB to a shared DB + one DB per account:

```
data/
├── shared.sqlite                    (registry + shared caches + operational state)
├── account_<hex_pubkey>.sqlite      (one per local account)
└── mdk_<hex_pubkey>/                (MDK's own per-account DB, unchanged)
```

Tables now in the per-account DB: `account_settings`, `account_follows`,
`accounts_groups`, `drafts`, `push_registrations`, `group_push_tokens`,
`published_key_packages`, `published_events`, `aggregated_messages`,
`message_delivery_status`, `media_references`, `mute_list`, account-scoped
`processed_events`.

Tables remaining in `shared.sqlite`: `accounts` (registry), `users`,
`relays`, `user_relays`, `cached_graph_users`, `group_information`,
`media_blobs` (shared blob cache), `relay_status`, `relay_events`, global
`processed_events`, `app_settings`.

Consequence: account deletion is `fs::remove_file` on the account DB plus
removing the MDK directory. No multi-table row cleanup. No chance of leftover
state.

### 5. SQLx migrations replaced with an in-tree Rust framework

`sqlx::migrate!` no longer drives schema. The Rust framework lets us:
- Apply migrations against either the shared DB or each per-account DB,
- Rebaseline the bootstrap (v17–v22 + v29 are now baked into
  `fresh_account_schema` per PR #790) so new accounts open a single `CREATE`
  rather than replay every historical migration,
- Run cross-DB ordering with explicit dependencies (see PR #785).

### 6. CLI extracted to a workspace crate

`crates/whitenoise-cli/` is now its own workspace member with its own
`Cargo.toml`. The core library no longer pulls in `clap`, `dirs`, or
`rpassword`. `wn` / `wnd` binaries live in the CLI crate. Shared deps
(`mdk-core`, `nostr-sdk`, `tokio`, …) are declared once in
`[workspace.dependencies]` so the core crate and CLI can't silently diverge
on git-pinned revisions.

### 7. BroadcastHub consolidation

The four structurally identical streaming managers (chat list, messages,
notifications, group state, user) are unified behind a generic
`BroadcastHub<K, V>` (Phase 17, PR #765). Streaming entry points haven't
changed for consumers.

---

## Phase log

| Phase | PR | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #743 | `AccountSession` + `AccountManager` scaffolding, startup restore, MDK caching |
| 2 | (PR included) | Per-account guards and cancellation moved to session |
| 3 / 3b | #753, #755, #756 | Scoped relay handles; `AccountInboxPlane` ownership on session |
| 4 | #754 | `AccountRepositories` scaffold |
| 5 | #761 | View pattern: drafts, follows, settings migrated |
| 6 + 7 | #760 | Message read/search + send/retry/projection write path; `message_delivery_status` scope bug fix |
| 8 | #763 | Group read operations |
| 9 | #766 | Group member/data mutation operations |
| 10 | #769 | `create_group` and welcome delivery on session |
| 11 | #772 | Group media operations on `MediaOps` |
| 12 | #764 | Memberships (`accounts_groups`) → `MembershipOps` |
| 13 | #767 | Push notification ops → `PushOps` |
| 14 | #768 | Key packages + chat list reads on session |
| 15 | #770 | Session-scoped event dispatch |
| 16a | #773 | `Arc<SharedServices>` holder (singleton still present) |

| 18b | #787 | `media_files` → `media_blobs` (shared) + `media_references` (per-account) |
| 18c | #786 | Simple per-account tables moved to per-account DB |
| 18d | #792 | Membership + push tables → per-account DB |
| 18e | #796 | Message projection tables + chat-list join logic → per-account DB |
| — | #783, #785, #790 | SQLx → Rust migration framework; ordering; v31 rebaseline |
| — | #789 | `media_references` to per-account DB |
| — | #810 | `mute_list` per-account (m0042 + m0043) |
| 19 | #774 | CLI extracted to `crates/whitenoise-cli` |
| Cleanup | #818 | Remove deprecated `Whitenoise` facades; migrate remaining callers to `AccountSession` |
| Master sync / fixes | #782, #801, #812, #816, #817, #820, #795 | Master integrations + fixes for push tokens, session-restore ordering, `file_metadata` BLOB decode, MIP-04 v2 integration tests |

---

## Breaking changes for downstream consumers

Consumers of the public Rust API (notably the Flutter app via FRB):

- `Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. Construct a `Whitenoise` at app
  init and hold a reference.
- Account-scoped methods are removed from `Whitenoise` and moved onto
  `AccountSession`. Call sites change from
  `wn.method(&account, …)` to `wn.session(account.pubkey)?.area().method(…)`.
- Account deletion now removes a single SQLite file rather than running
  multi-table cleanup.
- Storage layout on disk changes — see migration notes below.

## Migration / on-disk compatibility

- Existing single-DB installations are migrated forward by the Rust migration
  framework. Per-account tables are physically moved into per-account DBs as
  part of the 18-series migrations.
- The fresh-install schema is rebaselined to v31 (PR #790); fresh accounts no
  longer replay v17–v22 / v29 historical migrations.
- Cross-scope foreign keys (e.g. `accounts_groups → accounts`,
  `drafts → group_information`) are enforced at the application layer post-split.
  See the cross-scope FK audit in the module-level doc comments of
  `database/shared_db.rs` and `database/account_db.rs`.

---

## Testing

Testing transitions to a three-tier model (see
[`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md)):

- **Tier 1 — Unit tests:** in-memory `AccountDatabase` + individually
  constructed services. Cover services, repos, views, projection logic, chat
  list ordering, message aggregation, group membership CRUD, drafts, settings,
  follows, key-package lifecycle. Run with `just test`. Parallel, fast, no
  infrastructure.
- **Tier 2 — In-process integration (MockRelay):** full in-process Nostr
  relay (WebSocket + in-memory store + NIP-01/42). Multi-instance tests like
  "Alice sends, Bob receives" are now possible. Each test owns its own
  `Whitenoise` instances; no shared state.
- **Tier 3 — Docker integration tests:** retained only for scenarios that need
  a real Blossom media server (`chat_media_upload`). Run with `just int-test`.

The scenario-by-scenario migration map is in [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md).

## Test plan (for this PR)

- [ ] CI: fmt + clippy (`-D warnings`) + docs build clean
- [ ] CI: unit tests pass on Linux + macOS-latest + macOS-14
- [ ] CI: coverage non-regression check
- [ ] CI: integration tests (Docker) green
- [ ] Manual: fresh install on a clean data dir — identity create, join group,
      send/receive, restart, verify persistence
- [ ] Manual: upgrade from a master-shaped data dir — verify per-account DB
      split applies cleanly and no rows are lost (accounts, groups, drafts,
      follows, mute list, push registrations, message projections)
- [ ] Manual: account deletion removes only that account's DB + MDK directory
- [ ] Manual: parallel `just test` runs are stable (no singleton contention)
- [ ] Spot-check: no `Whitenoise::get_instance()` callers anywhere in `src/`
      or `crates/`

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Lands the **session and projection rearchitecture** — a refactor that
restructures White Noise around explicit account-scoped sessions, projection-owning
services, and per-account SQLite databases. The work was executed across 19 numbered
phases, each landed as its own reviewed PR; this PR merges the full series from
`arch-refactor` into `master`.

**Scope:** 44 commits · 337 files · +42,350 / −17,302 

The design is fully documented in-repo:

- [`docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md`](docs/session-projection-rearchitecture.md) — target architecture
- [`docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md`](docs/session-projection-implementation-plan.md) — phase-by-phase plan
- [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md) — three-tier test model


Closes #739.

---

## Why

The pre-refactor codebase had a single `Whitenoise` global singleton with ~25 fields
and `impl` blocks spread across 37+ files. That shape produced three structural
problems:

1. **"Where does this go?"** Core files had grown past 2,000 lines; contributors
   couldn't tell where new code belonged or whether something similar already existed.
2. **Account scope was a convention, not a guarantee.** Every account-mutating
   method accepted `pubkey: PublicKey` as an argument; the compiler couldn't catch a
   wrong-pubkey bug. `message_delivery_status` already had a real scope bug where
   sender-local state bled across accounts in the same group.
3. **The singleton blocked testing.** `Whitenoise::get_instance()` returned a
   process-wide static. Parallel tests with isolated state were impossible. Swapping
   a service for a test double was impossible. Integration tests required
   logout → sleep → reset-client → wipe-database → sleep between scenarios.

The relay-control-plane rearchitecture had already solved the same problem at the
transport layer (one shared `nostr-sdk::Client` split into four dedicated planes).
This PR applies the same treatment to the domain layer.

---

## What changes

### 1. `AccountSession` is the new account-scoped handle

Account-scoped state has a typed owner. Login creates a session; logout drops it.
Account identity is baked into the handle, not passed as an argument.

```rust
// before
whitenoise.send_message_to_group(&account, &group_id, content).await?;
whitenoise.leave_group(&account, &group_id).await?;
whitenoise.follow_user(&account, &target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.resolve_user(&pubkey).await?;

// after
let session = whitenoise.session(account_pubkey)?;
session.messages().send_to_group(&group_id, content).await?;
session.groups().leave(&group_id).await?;
session.social().follow_user(&target_pubkey).await?;
let user = whitenoise.shared().user_directory().resolve(&pubkey).await?;
```

`session.messages()`, `session.groups()`, etc. return lightweight `View<'_>` types
that borrow the session — no Arc cycles, no separate service construction. Views
live in `src/whitenoise/session/`, one file per concern.

### 2. Four explicit state categories

Every piece of state now belongs to exactly one of:

| Category | Owner | Mutation rule |
|---|---|---|
| MDK authority | `AccountSession.mdk` (cached `Arc<MDK<_>>`) | MDK only |
| Shared app state | `SharedServices` (user directory, relays, app settings, media blob cache, …) | Shared services own writes; sessions read |
| Account-scoped app state | `AccountSession.repos` over `AccountDatabase` | Session services only |
| Projections | Declared builder + reader pair | Builders write directly to projection tables, readers query |

### 3. The singleton is gone

`Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. `Whitenoise` is constructed at startup
(FRB init, CLI daemon, tests) and passed by reference. `OnceCell`/`OnceLock` are
now reserved for process-level concerns only (tracing init, keyring store).

### 4. Per-account SQLite databases

Storage moved from one shared DB to a shared DB + one DB per account:

```
data/
├── shared.sqlite                    (registry + shared caches + operational state)
├── account_<hex_pubkey>.sqlite      (one per local account)
└── mdk_<hex_pubkey>/                (MDK's own per-account DB, unchanged)
```

Tables now in the per-account DB: `account_settings`, `account_follows`,
`accounts_groups`, `drafts`, `push_registrations`, `group_push_tokens`,
`published_key_packages`, `published_events`, `aggregated_messages`,
`message_delivery_status`, `media_references`, `mute_list`, account-scoped
`processed_events`.

Tables remaining in `shared.sqlite`: `accounts` (registry), `users`,
`relays`, `user_relays`, `cached_graph_users`, `group_information`,
`media_blobs` (shared blob cache), `relay_status`, `relay_events`, global
`processed_events`, `app_settings`.

Consequence: account deletion is `fs::remove_file` on the account DB plus
removing the MDK directory. No multi-table row cleanup. No chance of leftover
state.

### 5. SQLx migrations replaced with an in-tree Rust framework

`sqlx::migrate!` no longer drives schema. The Rust framework lets us:
- Apply migrations against either the shared DB or each per-account DB,
- Rebaseline the bootstrap (v17–v22 + v29 are now baked into
  `fresh_account_schema` per PR #790) so new accounts open a single `CREATE`
  rather than replay every historical migration,
- Run cross-DB ordering with explicit dependencies (see PR #785).

### 6. CLI extracted to a workspace crate

`crates/whitenoise-cli/` is now its own workspace member with its own
`Cargo.toml`. The core library no longer pulls in `clap`, `dirs`, or
`rpassword`. `wn` / `wnd` binaries live in the CLI crate. Shared deps
(`mdk-core`, `nostr-sdk`, `tokio`, …) are declared once in
`[workspace.dependencies]` so the core crate and CLI can't silently diverge
on git-pinned revisions.

### 7. BroadcastHub consolidation

The four structurally identical streaming managers (chat list, messages,
notifications, group state, user) are unified behind a generic
`BroadcastHub<K, V>` (Phase 17, PR #765). Streaming entry points haven't
changed for consumers.

---

## Phase log

| Phase | PR | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #743 | `AccountSession` + `AccountManager` scaffolding, startup restore, MDK caching |
| 2 | (PR included) | Per-account guards and cancellation moved to session |
| 3 / 3b | #753, #755, #756 | Scoped relay handles; `AccountInboxPlane` ownership on session |
| 4 | #754 | `AccountRepositories` scaffold |
| 5 | #761 | View pattern: drafts, follows, settings migrated |
| 6 + 7 | #760 | Message read/search + send/retry/projection write path; `message_delivery_status` scope bug fix |
| 8 | #763 | Group read operations |
| 9 | #766 | Group member/data mutation operations |
| 10 | #769 | `create_group` and welcome delivery on session |
| 11 | #772 | Group media operations on `MediaOps` |
| 12 | #764 | Memberships (`accounts_groups`) → `MembershipOps` |
| 13 | #767 | Push notification ops → `PushOps` |
| 14 | #768 | Key packages + chat list reads on session |
| 15 | #770 | Session-scoped event dispatch |
| 16a | #773 | `Arc<SharedServices>` holder (singleton still present) |
| 16b | #779 | Singleton killed; `Whitenoise` is constructed and passed in |
| 16c | #780 | Post-singleton cleanup |
| 17 | #765 | `BroadcastHub` generic for streaming managers |
| 18a | #776 | `SharedDatabase` + `AccountDatabase` newtypes; cross-scope FK audit |
| 18b | #787 | `media_files` → `media_blobs` (shared) + `media_references` (per-account) |
| 18c | #786 | Simple per-account tables moved to per-account DB |
| 18d | #792 | Membership + push tables → per-account DB |
| 18e | #796 | Message projection tables + chat-list join logic → per-account DB |
| — | #783, #785, #790 | SQLx → Rust migration framework; ordering; v31 rebaseline |
| — | #789 | `media_references` to per-account DB |
| — | #810 | `mute_list` per-account (m0042 + m0043) |
| 19 | #774 | CLI extracted to `crates/whitenoise-cli` |
| Cleanup | #818 | Remove deprecated `Whitenoise` facades; migrate remaining callers to `AccountSession` |
| Master sync / fixes | #782, #801, #812, #816, #817, #820, #795 | Master integrations + fixes for push tokens, session-restore ordering, `file_metadata` BLOB decode, MIP-04 v2 integration tests |

---

## Breaking changes for downstream consumers

Consumers of the public Rust API (notably the Flutter app via FRB):

- `Whitenoise::get_instance()` is removed. Construct a `Whitenoise` at app
  init and hold a reference.
- Account-scoped methods are removed from `Whitenoise` and moved onto
  `AccountSession`. Call sites change from
  `wn.method(&account, …)` to `wn.session(account.pubkey)?.area().method(…)`.
- Account deletion now removes a single SQLite file rather than running
  multi-table cleanup.
- Storage layout on disk changes — see migration notes below.

## Migration / on-disk compatibility

- Existing single-DB installations are migrated forward by the Rust migration
  framework. Per-account tables are physically moved into per-account DBs as
  part of the 18-series migrations.
- The fresh-install schema is rebaselined to v31 (PR #790); fresh accounts no
  longer replay v17–v22 / v29 historical migrations.
- Cross-scope foreign keys (e.g. `accounts_groups → accounts`,
  `drafts → group_information`) are enforced at the application layer post-split.
  See the cross-scope FK audit in the module-level doc comments of
  `database/shared_db.rs` and `database/account_db.rs`.

---

## Testing

Testing transitions to a three-tier model (see
[`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md)):

- **Tier 1 — Unit tests:** in-memory `AccountDatabase` + individually
  constructed services. Cover services, repos, views, projection logic, chat
  list ordering, message aggregation, group membership CRUD, drafts, settings,
  follows, key-package lifecycle. Run with `just test`. Parallel, fast, no
  infrastructure.
- **Tier 2 — In-process integration (MockRelay):** full in-process Nostr
  relay (WebSocket + in-memory store + NIP-01/42). Multi-instance tests like
  "Alice sends, Bob receives" are now possible. Each test owns its own
  `Whitenoise` instances; no shared state.
- **Tier 3 — Docker integration tests:** retained only for scenarios that need
  a real Blossom media server (`chat_media_upload`). Run with `just int-test`.

The scenario-by-scenario migration map is in [`docs/testing-strategy.md`](docs/testing-strategy.md).

## Test plan (for this PR)

- [ ] CI: fmt + clippy (`-D warnings`) + docs build clean
- [ ] CI: unit tests pass on Linux + macOS-latest + macOS-14
- [ ] CI: coverage non-regression check
- [ ] CI: integration tests (Docker) green
- [ ] Manual: fresh install on a clean data dir — identity create, join group,
      send/receive, restart, verify persistence
- [ ] Manual: upgrade from a master-shaped data dir — verify per-account DB
      split applies cleanly and no rows are lost (accounts, groups, drafts,
      follows, mute list, push registrations, message projections)
- [ ] Manual: account deletion removes only that account's DB + MDK directory
- [ ] Manual: parallel `just test` runs are stable (no singleton contention)
- [ ] Spot-check: no `Whitenoise::get_instance()` callers anywhere in `src/`
      or `crates/`

issue.title: fix(media_files): decode file_metadata column as BLOB
issue.body: ## Symptom Migrated devices crash when sending or receiving messages in any chat that has media history. Flutter log: ``` SEVERE MessageService sendMessage FAILED error: ApiError.whitenoise(message: Database error: SQLx error: error occurred while decoding column "file_metadata": mismatched types; Rust type `core::option::Option` (as SQL type `TEXT`) is not compatible with SQL type `BLOB`) ``` Affects both send and receive because `MediaFile::find_by_hash` sits on every message path that touches a referenced media row. ## Root cause `ReferenceRow.file_metadata` in `src/whitenoise/database/media_files.rs` was declared `Option`, which sqlx maps to SQL `TEXT`. The `media_references.file_metadata` column is declared `BLOB` in every schema: - `m0013_media_blob_reference_split.rs:60` - `m0029_move_media_references.rs:50,173,254` - `rust_migrations/fresh_account_schema.sql:87` - `rust_migrations/fresh_schema.sql:124` Any production path that stored raw bytes there produced a BLOB-typed cell. sqlx's strict decoder then refuses the BLOB → `Option` coercion at `try_get`, before the existing `serde_json::from_str` deserializer can run. Not caused by the recent arch-refactor migrations (m0042/m0043). Latent code/schema mismatch surfaced by data shape present on migrated devices. ## Fix Read side only, single file (`src/whitenoise/database/media_files.rs`): - `ReferenceRow.file_metadata`: `Option` → `Option>` - `assemble()`: `serde_json::from_str(&s)` → `serde_json::from_slice(&s)` Write path at lines 341/379 (sqlx's `Json` adapter) stays untouched. Public `MediaFile.file_metadata: Option` shape stays untouched. The deserialized value round-trips through the same `FileMetadata` type. ## Compatibility Data on disk unchanged. The fix is decoder-side; existing BLOB-typed cells decode cleanly under the new field type. No migration. No schema change. ## Test plan - [x] Regression test added: `test_file_metadata_blob_column_roundtrip` forces a BLOB-typed cell via `CAST(? AS BLOB)`, asserts `typeof(file_metadata) = 'blob'` as a setup guard, then verifies `MediaFile::find_by_hash` round-trips `FileMetadata` fields - [x] `cargo test --lib database::media_files` — passes - [x] `just precommit-quick` — green ---

issue.title: remove 67 deprecated Whitenoise facades, migrate callers to AccountSession
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/b5218fa466fca7720a492509142d73979ab7d76bce0a6c1cbe26aca966b68a10.jpg) The `#[deprecated]` facades on `Whitenoise` have been around since 0.0.0 with notes that say "use `AccountSession::()` instead." A `push_notifications.rs` comment even promised they would be removed once callers migrated. They never were. This PR finishes the job. ## What changed * 67 deprecated public methods removed across 11 files (mute_list, drafts, account_settings, follows, chat_list, accounts_groups, key_packages, groups, groups/media, groups/publish, push_notifications). * Every caller now hits `AccountSession::()` directly. Production callers in `streaming.rs`, `accounts_groups::delete_chat`, `event_processor`, the key-package maintenance scheduler, `user_search`, and the chat-list image resolver are all migrated. Tests, benchmarks, and integration test cases follow. * Two facades did more than delegate. Their wrapped behavior moved into the session so FFI consumers see no change. `SettingsOps::update_notifications_enabled` now performs MIP-05 push-token reconciliation. `SocialOps::{follow_user, unfollow_user}` resolve users, write the follow row, and republish the follow list; the pure-DB `add_follow` and `remove_follow` are gone. * Dead-code collateral: `Whitenoise::resolve_member_key_package`, `map_mdk_add_members_error`, `share_push_token_to_joined_groups`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_GROUP_PUBLISHES`, `publish_event_with_retry`, the orphan `publish_and_merge_commit`. `KeyPackageLookup::Incompatible` is now a unit variant since no production caller read the embedded error. Two projection helpers (`find_member_missing_required_proposal`, `marmot_key_package_capabilities`) stay under `#[cfg(test)]` since their unit tests still validate the projection logic. ## Diff 72 files, +2249 / -2901 (about 650 lines deleted net). Zero `#[deprecated]` and zero `#[allow(deprecated)]` remain in `src/`. ## Verification `just check` passes (fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, docs, no `#[allow(dead_code)]`). Unit tests need Docker; the relay-dependent failures on my machine match the known-flaky behavior without `just docker-up`. The marmot finally took out the trash. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Refactor** * Consolidated account operations to use session-scoped APIs instead of deprecated account-based facades across groups, chat lists, drafts, follows, mute lists, and key package management. [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/818)

**Avoid `unwrap()` after an already-guarded session lookup.**

At Line 95, `require_session(...).unwrap()` can panic and bypass your graceful error handling path, even though `session` was already resolved at Lines 58-68. Reuse that existing `session` for group membership calls.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-        match whitenoise
-            .require_session(&account.pubkey)
-            .unwrap()
-            .groups()
-            .members(&ag.mls_group_id)
-        {
+        match session.groups().members(&ag.mls_group_id) {
```
</details>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@src/whitenoise/user_search/graph.rs` around lines 93 - 98, The code is
calling whitenoise.require_session(&account.pubkey).unwrap() again which can
panic; instead reuse the previously-resolved session variable (the one obtained
around Lines 58–68) when calling groups().members(&ag.mls_group_id) (i.e.
replace require_session(...).unwrap().groups().members(...) with
session.groups().members(...)); if the earlier session might be out of scope,
pass it into the current function or propagate a clear error instead of
unwrapping so group membership uses the already-validated session and cannot
panic.
```
